_comment: TypeScript / JavaScript rules. Extracted from the v0.12 typescript-node templates, with the rationale that was previously implicit and the checks that previously lived in analyze/SKILL.md's pattern library.

rules.title: No default exports
rules.rationale: A default export is renamed silently at every import site, so a rename refactor cannot be verified mechanically. Named exports also make re-export barrels diffable and let editors auto-import reliably.

check.note: Vue SFCs and Svelte components export the component as default by convention — excluded deliberately.

rules.title: Tests live next to their source
rules.statement: **Tests next to source**: `foo.ts` → `foo.test.ts`. Integration tests in `tests/`.
rules.rationale: A test beside its subject is found when the subject is edited, and moves with it. A parallel test tree drifts: files get renamed on one side only, and nobody notices the orphan.

check.note: Reported as partial coverage, not a violation — not every file warrants a test.

rules.title: No `any`
rules.rationale: `any` disables checking for every expression it touches, and it spreads: one `any` at a boundary silently untypes everything downstream. `unknown` keeps the value opaque until it is actually narrowed, which is the check you wanted.

check.note: Declaration files are excluded — third-party shims frequently need `any`. Known false positive: prose containing `: any` inside a comment or string matches too (ripgrep has no comment awareness). Verified on a real project, where the single hit was the comment `Crude heuristic: any CJK char`. Report matches with enough context for the reader to dismiss them.

rules.title: No `console.log` in committed code
rules.statement: **No `console.log` in committed code.** Use a logger.
rules.rationale: `console.log` has no level, no structure and no destination control, so it cannot be filtered in production and frequently leaks values that should not be in logs. A logger gives all three.

rules.title: Throw Error subclasses, not strings
rules.statement: **Errors are typed.** Throw `Error` subclasses, not strings.
rules.rationale: A thrown string has no stack trace, which removes the single most useful piece of debugging information at exactly the moment it is needed. `instanceof` on an Error subclass also lets callers handle failures selectively.

rules.title: No unexplained `eslint-disable`
rules.statement: No `eslint-disable` without a comment explaining why.
rules.rationale: A silent disable is indistinguishable from a mistake, so nobody dares remove it and it outlives the problem it worked around. The explanation is what makes it removable later.

check.note: A violation is a disable with no justification on the same line.

rules.title: Descriptive test names
rules.rationale: A failing test's name is the entire bug report in CI output. `test 3 fails` costs a debugging session that `should reject expired tokens when the clock has advanced` would have prevented.

check.reason: naming quality is not mechanically decidable

rules.title: Clean up side effects
rules.rationale: Uncleaned state is the mechanism behind order-dependent suites (UNI-005): the leak is created by one test and only observed by another, so the failure blames innocent code.

check.reason: requires knowing which setup created state

rules.title: No real time in tests
rules.statement: No tests that depend on real wall-clock time without freezing it (`vi.useFakeTimers()` / `jest.useFakeTimers()`).
rules.rationale: A test that reads the real clock fails at midnight, at a month boundary, in another timezone, or under CI load — always intermittently, and always for a reason unrelated to the code under test.

check.note: Heuristic: flags real-clock reads in test files, including legitimate ones inside a frozen-timer block. Reported for review, not as a hard violation.

rules.title: No snapshots of non-deterministic data
rules.statement: No snapshots of components with non-deterministic data.
rules.rationale: A snapshot containing a timestamp, a random id or an unordered map fails on the next run for no reason, and the fix everyone reaches for — updating the snapshot — silently accepts whatever else changed with it.

check.reason: determinism of snapshot content is not statically decidable
